hooks.text: This deep blue world sixty-four light-years away holds no peaceful oceans.
A planet sixty-four light-years from Earth looks deceptively like a blue marble.
Could a deep blue planet sixty-four light-years away harbor peaceful oceans?

title: The Blue Planet That Rains Sideways Glass
description: HD 189733 b looks like a peaceful blue marble from afar, but its atmosphere is a scorching inferno. Powerful winds whip molten silicate particles sideways through toxic clouds.

beats.text: This deep blue world sixty-four light-years away holds no peaceful oceans.
beats.visual: Artist's impression of exoplanet HD 189733 b, NASA, 2013

beats.text: When French astronomers discovered HD 189733 b in October 2005, its azure shade seemed familiar.
beats.visual: Haute-Provence Observatory dome where HD 189733 b was discovered, 2005

beats.text: Most people imagine water, but this planet is a scorching gas giant larger than Jupiter.
beats.visual: Artist's comparison of Jupiter and hot Jupiter exoplanet HD 189733 b, 2007

beats.text: Tidally locked to its parent star, atmospheric temperatures reach roughly twelve hundred Kelvin.
beats.visual: Spitzer Space Telescope global temperature map of exoplanet HD 189733 b, 2007

beats.text: The cobalt color is actually caused by high-altitude haze scattering light.
beats.visual: Diagram illustrating Rayleigh scattering in planetary atmospheres, 2013

beats.text: Those clouds are composed of silicates, the exact mineral family of glass and sand.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope illustration of clouds on HD 189733 b, 2013

beats.text: Powerful jet streams blow these tiny silicate particles sideways across the planet.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of supersonic silicate winds on HD 189733 b, NASA, 2015

beats.text: To make matters worse, the lethal atmosphere reeks like rotten eggs from hydrogen sulfide.
beats.visual: James Webb Space Telescope rendering in deep space, NASA, 2022
queries: James Webb Space Telescope artist concept

beats.text: Nature disguised a terrifying storm of flying glass inside a serene blue marble.
beats.visual: Artist's rendering of deep blue exoplanet HD 189733 b in orbit, 2013

better_than_last: Replaced technical meteorological terminology in late beats with vivid sensory details like rotten egg odors and sideways flying glass to maintain audience engagement through the finish.
